claims.text: In C# 14 a class implements an interface by naming it after the colon and implementing every member that has no default body (else CS0535), or by deriving from a class that does; EmailNotifier implements INotifier through NotifierBase.

claims.text: In C# 14 an abstract class cannot be created with new (new NotifierBase() -> CS0144); besides abstract methods it can hold fields and implemented methods, and a derived class inherits every member except constructors and finalizers.

claims.text: A variable declared with a class or interface type accepts an object whose class is, derives from or implements that type; an object of a class that only implements INotifier cannot be assigned to NotifierBase (CS0029).

claims.text: Code holding a variable declared as INotifier may call Send on it because INotifier declares Send; EmailNotifier and SmsNotifier objects can be assigned to it because NotifierBase implements INotifier and they derive from NotifierBase.

claims.text: A class that implements INotifier directly, without deriving from NotifierBase, can be assigned to an INotifier variable, and a Send call through it runs only that class's own Send.
